question_text: How does the copper weight (thickness) of a PCB trace affect its parasitic properties?
answer_text: Heavier copper primarily decreases the trace's DC and AC resistance.
explanation_text: Using 2 oz copper instead of 1 oz copper doubles the cross-sectional height of the trace. This provides a larger vertical conduit for current to flow, significantly lowering resistance. It has a negligible effect on capacitance and only a very minor effect on inductance.
bonus_question_text: What does "1 oz copper" actually mean in physical dimensions?
bonus_answer_text: It is the thickness resulting from pressing exactly 1 ounce of copper evenly over 1 square foot of area, which equals roughly 1.37 mils (35 μm) in thickness.
